body:
UrlProtocol host shutdown can fail when a full native event-loop queue rejects close work or completion delivery. This change supports the owner's request: "Use codex 6.1-sol to drive url://handoff/handoffs/hf-2026-10-02-make-kompile-s-shared-caches-safe-for-concurrent-runs-reproduce-the-hang-stale-lock-replay-and-single-flight-defects-and-fix-them-upstream-so-no-campaign-needs-an-external-build-lock to completion".

Factory shutdown ends listen/dial admission, closes owned listeners using their original bind values, drains registered roots through `closeProtocolRoot()`, and then attempts native stop even when an earlier stage failed. Listener operation futures remain detached from their private owners. Admitted connection handlers drain before the root snapshot; later handshakes cannot enter the network, and a handshake arriving after a failed native stop retains that failure without another physical close.

R992 exposed two further defects. The transport now owns a deep copy of a listener's bind value, including the caller's component byte arrays, and passes that same value to native listen and later unlisten. Dial values are copied before admission; native dial initiation and its asynchronous preparation continuation cross the same shutdown boundary, so an input read cannot create a raw channel after completed shutdown.

**R992 finding 5 remains unresolved; this PR is not ready to merge.** The public `testR992FailedListenerCloseStillEndsAcceptorLoop` probe fails on the reviewed head: native `PlainNettyTransport.close()` reaches its private acceptor-group shutdown only through `allClosed.thenCompose`, which is skipped when a listener close fails. That resource is owned upstream. No downstream cleanup workaround or new artifact publication was made; a fixed upstream artifact is still needed. The failing probe and XML are preserved in the [F992b evidence](https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/UrlProtocol/tree/wip/F992b-evidence-20261029/evidence/F992b).

Current main already adopted snapshot-41 and explicit retirement retries in https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/UrlProtocol/pull/945, and the drain fixture fixes in https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/UrlProtocol/pull/975 and https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/UrlProtocol/pull/978. This PR retains snapshot-41 and replaces the closed https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/UrlProtocol/pull/962. An earlier lane brief requested a snapshot-25 backport; that artifact is unused by current UrlProtocol, and its completed publication record was closed with the [required explanation](https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/jvm-libp2p/pull/74#issuecomment-6493023443).

Validation on the new product change:

- The bind-list and held-dial probes fail on unchanged `10fb58f0`; the added bind-byte probe also fails after its compile error was corrected. All four actionable new tests pass with the fixes.
- The 17 actionable tests (13 original PR tests plus four added tests) pass **510/510** across exactly 30 single-attempt repetitions per name, 510 attempts, no retries.
- The upstream acceptor-loop probe fails **0/30** at the same cleanup assertion, 30 attempts, no retries. The complete requested 18-name register is therefore **510/540**, with finding 5 visibly unresolved.
- All three R992 mutations and three address/dial mutations are caught: **6/6**, one attempt each, with the expected behavior failure and no compilation failures.
- Final post-rebase check: **17/17** passing tests, 17 attempts, no retries, on `314e77bf5895352f4e7f1235bebaa069ec373efc`.
- Binding M8 makes Actions the full-suite gate. New-head Actions XML is pending; the earlier reviewed head's green result is not reused. No remote suite was submitted manually.

Existing-main test edits: **none**. F992b also leaves all 13 original PR test files unchanged and adds four permanent tests: caller bind-list mutation, caller bind-byte mutation, held dial input, and late handshake after failed native close. The separate acceptor-loop diagnostic remains failing in evidence, not a claimed passing test. No timeout, iteration count, or assertion on main was weakened. Earlier work on this PR corrected its own new listener-failure test from expecting a second native close to expecting the retained first failure; it kept the original error identity and immutability assertions and provided explicit cleanup.

No merge, enqueue, deployment or publication is authorized by this update.
